title: Prorated billing mismatch after interleaved rollback during Dedicated capacity evictions
creator: Marco Rivera
description: Summary: Several Dedicated customers reported unexpected proration credits applied to invoices after transient node evictions during an autoscaling event. The credits are not explained by any documented refund rule and lead to downstream AR reconciliation failures. Scope: observed in Dedicated clusters only; Hosted and Private regions not affected. Initial pattern suggests the credits correlate with requests that were routed to a node which started a rollback path while prefix-KV reconciliation and usage aggregation were simultaneously replayed.
reproduction_steps: Provision a Dedicated pool and enable autoscaling with eviction policy 'best-effort'
Send a mix of streaming and REST generation requests that produce overlapping KV cache warmups (prefix hits) and persistent streaming sessions
Trigger a scale-down so a worker shuts down while a subset of requests are in-flight and retries are routed to fallback nodes
Observe billing ledger entries for the affected tenant for the current billing epoch via the metering-export dashboard
Verify that prorated credits outsize the expected retry/fallback credit rules in the ledger and invoice export
observed_behavior: Meters emitted a negative delta for the tenant on the billing epoch; accounting pipeline applied a prorated credit that matched a fraction of tokens generated across interleaved sessions. The ledger shows both the original token entries and a later corrective credit; the credit amount does not match any single rollback/duplicate token rule and appears to have been computed from a partial session window aggregation produced during concurrent replay and eviction handling.
hypothesis: Race between the evicting node's local batch accounting flush and the central rollup aggregator causes double-attribution of a partial token window. When the eviction triggers a rollback path, the central aggregator receives both the local pre-eviction counts and a replayed coalesced delta from the fallback node. The reconciliation job sees an overlap and applies a prorated correction using a heuristic designed for gap-filling, but that heuristic misclassifies overlapping windows as eligible for customer credit rather than idempotent suppression.
mitigation_steps: Deploy emergency guard: disable the 'proactive prorate' heuristic in metering-rollup service via feature flag (ff_disable_proactive_prorate=true)
Apply hotfix to rollback path to mark replayed deltas with replay_origin=eviction so aggregator can identify and suppress duplicates
Notify affected customers with interim statement explaining temporary credits and that financial reconciliation is in progress
Backfill corrected ledger entries for the last 24 hours using a conservative suppress-duplicates pass and publish adjusted invoice exports to finance
long_term_fixes: Redesign rollup reconciliation to use a deterministic idempotency token per session-window generated at proxy ingress (rather than heuristic overlap), and surface those tokens through the eviction/replay lifecycle
Enhance KV cache warmup telemetry to include window identifiers so replayed prefix hits can be correlated without relying on time-based heuristics
Add unit+integration tests that simulate interleaved eviction+replay across Dedicated clusters and assert no net negative credits are produced
Update runbook: include explicit steps for customers on Dedicated plans when scale-down eviction occurs and ensure Console exposes transient ledger preview during graceful shutdowns
acceptance_criteria: Feature flag ff_disable_proactive_prorate reverted safely after tests and replaced by deterministic suppression logic
No new prorated negative credits observed across a 72-hour canary in Dedicated clusters under synthetic eviction load
Backfilled ledger adjustments reconciled with Finance and customer-facing notices delivered
Automated E2E tests added to CI that reproduce the race condition and fail if negative credits are generated
qa_plan: Create a canary Dedicated pool in staging; run the eviction test harness which alternates scale-down events under heavy streaming+prefix workloads. Validate metering-export and invoice-export against a golden reference that never includes negative credit entries. Run the canary for 72 hours and escalate if any divergence is detected.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR with idempotency token generation and suppression logic behind a feature flag. 2) Roll out to a small Dedicated tenant cohort (5 tenants) with tight monitoring. 3) If stable for 48 hours, expand to all Dedicated clusters. 4) Once stable, flip flag and remove legacy heuristic.
